source: Project Gutenberg catalogue, publishers, libraries, archives and marketplaces

categories.title: Fiction
categories.blurb: Novels and stories that fell out of copyright: the shelf that still sets the shape of the novel.

categories.title: Poetry
categories.blurb: Verse from epic to sonnet, with the translations that carried it between languages.

categories.title: Drama
categories.blurb: Plays written to be spoken, from tragedy to drawing-room comedy.

categories.title: Philosophy
categories.blurb: Arguments about knowledge, ethics and the good life, in editions free to copy.

categories.title: Science and nature
categories.blurb: Natural history, astronomy, physics, medicine and mathematics as they were written.

categories.title: History and biography
categories.blurb: Chronicles, lives and memoirs, with the biases of their century intact.

categories.title: Adventure and travel
categories.blurb: Sea stories, voyages and expeditions — the books that invented the travel narrative.

categories.title: Mystery and crime
categories.blurb: Detectives, ghosts and crime, from the penny dreadful to the locked room.

categories.title: Children and fairy tales
categories.blurb: Fairy tales, nursery rhymes and books written for readers who are still learning.

categories.title: Romance
categories.blurb: Love stories, from the epistolary novel to the courtship plot.

categories.title: Essays and letters
categories.blurb: Essays, letters and speeches: the short forms where an argument is made in public.

categories.title: Humour and satire
categories.blurb: Satire, wit and comic writing, from the essay to the stage.

categories.title: Religion and scripture
categories.blurb: Scripture, theology, mysticism and the study of religion, from the King James Bible to the Golden Bough.

categories.title: Free textbooks and manuals
categories.blurb: Authors and foundations that publish the whole book online, without a paywall, a login or a trial.

categories.title: Free audio · LibriVox
categories.blurb: Volunteers reading public-domain books aloud. The catalogue is uneven, the recordings are free, and the whole archive is downloadable.

categories.title: Borrow · libraries and archives
categories.blurb: A free library card is still the cheapest way to read a book that is in copyright; these are the shelves that lend digitally.

categories.title: Free comics and magazines
categories.blurb: The comics that fell out of copyright or were never renewed, plus the web platforms that publish for free and pay by advertising.

categories.title: Indie and pay-what-you-want
categories.blurb: The middle of the spectrum: a price the author sets, a price you choose, or a few euros for a book no publisher would have taken.

categories.title: Subscription · reading
categories.blurb: One monthly fee, a catalogue instead of a purchase. Cheap per book if you read a lot, expensive if you do not.

categories.title: Subscription · audio
categories.blurb: The same bargain for ears: a credit or a catalogue each month, and the book is only yours while you pay.

categories.title: New releases · bought outright
categories.blurb: The book costs what the publisher says, and it stays yours. Hardback first, paperback a year later, ebook on the same day.

categories.title: Academic and professional
categories.blurb: The expensive end: research monographs, journals and reference works, usually bought by a library rather than a person.

categories.title: Reference · dictionaries and style
categories.blurb: The books nobody reads from cover to cover and everybody needs open: definitions, usage, citation and the rules of the house.

categories.title: Rare · antiquarian and collectors
categories.blurb: First editions, signed copies and manuscripts. The price is whatever the last two bidders agreed on, and the condition is the whole argument.
